programmes.d: The body of a wealthy American businessman was found in his rental car. Teeth and bone fragments were the only remains. When the victim's wife files an insurance claim for $7 million, investigators seek the help of a renowned forensic anthropologist.
The 1987 disappearance of Houston resident Tracy Jo Shine is recalled.
Police investigate a missing college girl and discover her double life: attending school by day and working as a call-girl by night. Her body is found and investigators find her killer.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.

When convenience store employee Wanda Mason is found dead, investigators find the entire murder has been caught on the store's security camera. But the image of the killer is so degraded it seems impossible to positively identify him.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine. Michael Hutchinson, 32, was later found guilty in the slaying.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.

The victim had been sexually assaulted and stabbed to death on the beach. A pair of men's tennis shoes was discovered near her body. Police were sure that if they found the man who fit the shoes, they would also find the man who committed the crime.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.
In 1996, Indiana police identified Richard Alexander as the “River Park Rapist” who assaulted four women that year. Later, DNA analysis casts doubt on his conviction.
A jeweler's search through old sales records helps police find likely suspects in a couple's murder.

When Scott Dunn goes missing, police spray his bedroom with Luminol and uncover a scene of horrific violence. Now investigators face a daunting task: proving that Scott Dunn had been murdered without a body, a witness or a murder weapon.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.

When a woman disappeared without a trace, there were two possible explanations: kidnapping or murder. Careful investigation, a forensic artist and DNA profiling enabled police to find a single suspect, who was known to prey upon vulnerable women.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body.

In 1991, a high school girl vanished after attending a party. The prime suspect had two alibi witnesses for the night she disappeared. A solid alibi can often overcome circumstantial evidence, but forensic evidence is another matter.
The sensitive nose of a forensic examiner sniffs out murder.

When police find the body of 11-year-old Krista Harrison, there are few clues to the killer's identity. But authorities are intrigued by unusual orange fibers embedded in clothing found near the victim.
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.
When a successful stockbroker doesn't return home after a late shift, his wife reports him missing.
The only clue recovered from a shooting is a twelve-guage shotgun.

No one in a quiet residential community saw anything unusual the day one of their neighbors was brutally attacked and murdered. Fingerprints found at the crime scene and surveillance video helped investigators to apprehend the presumed killer.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause the deaths of three people.

On September 17, 1984, in a suburb of Tucson, Arizona, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home on her pink bicycle to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned, but her slightly damaged bicycle was found nearby.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.
In 1995, when off-duty Maine State Trooper Vicky Gardner is attacked by Steven Fortin during a routine stop, it triggers a chain of events which jumpstart a stalled murder case in New Jersey.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.

In 2007, the Florida mobile home of Effie and Michael Ratley catches fire. Michael heroically rescues his wife and infant son. A month later, his wife is found beaten to death in a bedroom of his parents' home.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers.

A man disappears one year to the day after beginning an affair with his friend's wife. 15 years later, with the help of a metal detector, police find evidence that would prove what had happened and who was responsible.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica.
When a hit-and-run boating accident caused the death of a popular young man, investigators faced the daunting task of searching for one boat among 1200 others.
An examination of the 2002 DC area shooting spree that resulted in ten murders.
A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial.

When a 9-year-old girl goes missing, police and volunteers spend weeks searching for her. A psychic's vision leads to a field where her body is discovered, along with what investigators hope is enough evidence to find her killer.
Notepad points to kidnapper.
In 1989, the dead bodies of Joan Rogers and her two teenage daughters were found floating in Tampa Bay.
Debate over cause of death.
In 1992, Laura Houghteling disappeared from her Bethesda home and was never seen again. Forensic scientists use evidence from her bedroom to direct police to a prime suspect.
A killer leaves the scene with the genetic fingerprint of his victim.

A human skeleton was discovered in the North Carolina marshlands. When investigators learned she'd been dead for 18 months, they knew it would be difficult to find out who she was, let alone who killed her.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.
After a Philadelphia Convention, 180 Legionnaires contract pneumonia-like symptoms and 29 of them die. The determination of one scientist helps identify the cause of this deadly disease.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later.

A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has a perfect alibi. To determine time of death, investigators need to know when the victim ate his last meal. An endocrinologist, a forensic botanist and a short-order cook answer their question.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.
When court clerk Peter Porco doesn't report to work in November 2004, a courts officer is ordered to the Porcos' family home in Bethlehem, NY.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.
A murder trail turned cold, until police got a call from a woman whose husband, Gerald Powers, had a criminal past and a fondness for Chevy Berettas.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.
In 1962, the small town residents of Hanford, California lost their sense of peace when one of their own, 15-year-old Marlene Miller, was murdered.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.

Police discover a bullet-riddled car, a missing driver and no witnesses. Had the victim been abducted or was she dead? The answers are found in a unique clue, so tiny it was measured in millionths of a meter.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.

A fifteen-year-old boy dies from a mysterious gunshot wound to the head while sitting in the lobby of his father's gun club. Ballistics, laser technology, made-to-scale models and the latest in forensic animation are used to find the cause.
A pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom.
When two women went missing and were later found brutally murdered, police wondered if they were victims of a hate crime.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a murder crime scene.
A security guard disappeared from his post without a trace; his remains were found a year later in a remote campsite.
A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has an almost perfect alibi.
When a college student vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety and their own.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.

An investigation into the murder of a World War II veteran slowed to a halt when the prime suspect had a solid alibi. But a lucky break led to a shady character who wore distinctive boots and had a sweet tooth.
In 1988, the body of a young woman was discovered in an Ohio river.
Crystal Faye Todd's case is examined; the popular high school student was raped and murdered.

In rural Canada, Dr. John Schneeberger is accused of sedating and sexually assaulting one of his female patients and his step daughter. DNA tests demonstrate that the doctor is innocent, but the patient insists that he sedated and raped her.
Police discovered the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife.
When a man is gunned down in his own garage, investigators use science to unravel a twisted tale of lust, greed and deception.
More than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a Boy Scout Camp near Farmington, Missouri. Facial reconstruction aids the investigators in this case.
A woman is found dead from a gunshot wound and police suspect her husband.

A married couple decided to escape the cold of winter with a mini-vacation in Key West. The wife went missing and police searched every square inch of the island; they found nothing but a pair of sandals which might have belonged to her.
In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with $500,000 in gold coins.
The bodies of several women are found on a remote hill in California. The police get a break when a prostitute escapes and is able to identify her attacker and his automobile.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
Authorities track a kidnapper who let his victim write a last will and informed the family of her murder. A phone number written on a previous page left a lasting impression, which helped to convict.
In 1984, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box.
In 1969, 25-year-old phone operator Diane Maxwell was raped and murdered. Her brother promised he'd find out who was responsible and bring the killer to justice.
A victim's knowledge of forensic evidence leads police to her abductor.
On October 15, 1985, two bomb explosions rocked Salt Lake City and resulted in two deaths. A third explosion occurred the next day; this time, the victim survived.
The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered among garbage.
The prime suspect had a criminal record and his driver's license was found at the scene of a brutal double homicide.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.

Residents of Noel, Missouri were stunned to learn that their bank had been robbed and the bank president was missing. His body was later found floating in a lake, securely bound to a chair with duct tape.
Forensic developments reveal new facts in the case of a man convicted of sexual assault.

A man tells police he shot an intruder who had attacked and murdered his wife. The husband paints a tragic picture and is dubbed a hero. Four years later, forensic evidence leads police to re-examine the motives of this so-called hero.
The murder of a couple puzzles investigators until the victims' dog leads police to the killer.

Nancy Newman and her two daughters are found brutally murdered. The crime scene has no shortage of evidence, but investigators cannot find a conclusive link to their prime suspect. To solve the puzzle, an FBI analyst designs a unique experiment.
Soon after becoming pregnant, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates.

A behavioral profile caused the Baton Rouge Police Department to search for the wrong man. The real perpetrator may have eluded arrest, had it not been for a molecular biologist who painted DNA picture of the suspect.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas.
Police are dispatched to the scene of a shooting and discover the victim's husband is one of their own: a homicide detective who says his wife accidentally shot herself in the head.
An abandoned, still-running car leads investigators to a body with unusual marks.

In 1993, the state of Florida was known for more than just Disney World. Worldwide attention focused on a rash of robberies which targeted tourists. Some vacationers were killed in these attacks, but some fought and survived.
Police uncover deleted computer files during an investigation.

A killer tries to incinerate everything that could link him to his crime. But in doing so, he inadvertently creates new forensic evidence. Detectives employ a technique never before used in a criminal investigation to bring it to light.
A suspicious neighbor gives police a break in a cold case.
